_meta.note: harvest months drive the ENSO seasonal alignment in build_enso_model.py
_meta.source: USDA IPAD crop calendars (FAO/GIEWS + FAS/GMA), read from Wayback-archived images; IPAD itself is retired

unreadable.reason: The Soybean row on the Indonesia calendar is drawn as a single green (planting) bar Oct-Dec with no mid-season or harvest bar, so no harvest months can be read.

barley.note: Orange occupies only the last ~1 column (Dec). Real Argentine barley harvest runs Dec-Jan; the image only clearly shows Dec.

corn.note: Orange left edge is at the Mar/Apr gridline; could be read as Mar-Jun. Grey (mid-season) covers Jan-Mar.

millet.note: LOW CONFIDENCE on the right edge: the orange band ends right around the Aug/Sep gridline, which is exactly the ONI alignment boundary. Bulk of the band is May-Aug. Argentine millet is a negligible crop.

sorghum.note: Green band Nov-Dec with grey lead-in from Oct; planting could be read as Oct-Dec.

soybeans.note: Chose 'Soybean (First)' row - first-crop soybeans dominate national production. 'Soybean (Second)' row plants Dec-Jan and harvests Apr-Jun.

wheat.note: Orange appears at the far right (Nov/Dec) AND as a small sliver in Jan, i.e. harvest wraps the year end. Bulk is Dec. Straddles the Aug/Sep ONI split only in the sense that Dec-Jan spans two calendar years - treat as Dec.

corn.note: Chose 'Corn (Centre-South, Second)' = safrinha, which is now ~75% of Brazilian maize. 'Corn (Centre-South, First)' plants Oct-Dec and harvests Feb-Jul; 'Corn (North-East)' plants Mar-May and harvests Oct-Dec. First and second crop both fall in the Jan-Aug ONI bucket, so the choice is low-risk.

rice.note: Chose 'Rice (Centre-South)' - Rio Grande do Sul is ~70% of Brazilian rice. 'Rice (North and Northeast)' plants Jan-Feb and harvests Jun-Aug.

sorghum.note: Two green blocks - one Oct-Dec and one Jan-Feb - so planting wraps the year end. Orange left edge sits on the Mar/Apr gridline.

soybeans.note: Grey (mid-season) covers Jan-Feb, orange starts at the Feb/Mar gridline; could be read as Feb-May.

wheat.note: Chose 'Wheat (Centre-South, Winter)' (Parana). 'Wheat (Rio Grande do Sul, Winter)' plants May-Jun and harvests Oct-Dec. Both are in the Sep-Dec ONI bucket.

barley.note: Barley (Meher). Same bar extents as the wheat row.

corn.note: Corn (Meher) - the main long-rains season. The only other cereal season shown is a pooled 'Cereals (Belg)' row (plant Feb-Mar, harvest Jun-Aug), which is a small minority of Ethiopian output.

millet.note: Millet (Meher). A small orange sliver also appears in Jan, i.e. the harvest tail runs Oct-Jan.

sorghum.note: Sorghum (Meher). Same bar extents as the maize row.

corn.note: Chose Corn (Rainy Region) - the main wet-season maize crop. Corn (Dry Region) plants May-Jul and harvests Aug-Oct.

rice.note: Chose Rice (1st) - the main wet-season crop, which carries the Feb-Apr national harvest peak. Rice (2nd) plants Apr-May and harvests Jul-Aug; Rice (3rd) plants Aug-Sep and harvests Nov-Dec.

corn.note: Chose Corn (Kharif) - ~65-70% of Indian maize. Corn (Rabi) plants Sep-Dec and harvests Jan-May.

millet.note: Chose Pearl Millet (Kharif) = bajra, the dominant millet. Pearl Millet (Rabi) plants Jan-Feb and harvests Apr-May.

rice.note: Chose Rice (Kharif) - kharif is ~85% of Indian rice. The green planting band is very wide (Feb-Aug) because it pools all of India; main sowing is Jun-Jul. A small orange sliver also appears in Jan, i.e. the kharif harvest tail runs Sep-Jan. Rice (Rabi) plants Dec-Jan and harvests Apr-May.

sorghum.note: WARNING - genuine two-season split with the two seasons in DIFFERENT ONI buckets. Chose Sorghum (Kharif): plant Jun-Jul, harvest Nov-Dec (Sep-Dec bucket). Sorghum (Rabi) plants Oct-Nov and harvests Mar-Apr (Jan-Aug bucket) and is of comparable national size (rabi jowar in Maharashtra/Karnataka is roughly half of Indian sorghum production and in recent years the larger half by area). Do not treat this entry as settled.

soybeans.note: Only a Soybean (Kharif) row exists. Unambiguous.

wheat.note: Only a Wheat (Rabi) row exists. Orange band Feb-Jun; bulk of the Indian wheat harvest is Mar-Apr.

corn.note: Chose Corn (Long Rain) - the long-rains crop is ~80% of Kenyan maize. Green band starts in late Mar. Corn (Short Rain) plants Oct-Nov and harvests Mar-Apr.

millet.note: Identical bar extents to the sorghum and rice rows.

rice.note: Identical bar extents to the sorghum and millet rows.

sorghum.note: Identical bar extents to the millet and rice rows.

wheat.note: Green band starts later than the other cereals, around mid-May.

barley.note: Orange band Mar-Apr; green Oct-Nov with a grey tail through Dec.

corn.note: Single Corn row pooling Pakistan's spring and autumn maize, hence the wide green band.

millet.note: Same bar extents as the sorghum row.

wheat.note: Wheat (Winter), the only wheat row. Orange right edge only just crosses into Jun; could be read as Apr-May.

corn.note: WARNING - the orange band on Corn (Main) starts mid-Jul and ends on the Sep/Oct gridline, so it straddles the Jan-Aug vs Sep-Dec ONI split. Chose Corn (Main) = wet season. Corn (Second Crop) plants Oct-Dec and harvests Feb-May.

rice.note: Chose Rice (Main) = wet season. Orange left edge sits inside Sep near the Sep/Oct gridline, so harvest could be read as Sep-Dec; either reading is in the Sep-Dec ONI bucket. Rice (Second Crop) plants Oct-Dec and harvests Feb-Apr.

corn.note: Chose Corn (Wet) - the dominant Thai maize crop. Corn (Dry) plants Nov and harvests Feb.

rice.note: Chose Rice (Wet) - the main wet-season crop, ~70%+ of Thai rice. Rice (Late Wet) plants Nov-Dec and harvests Feb-Mar. The Rice (Dry) row is drawn with an implausibly long orange band running roughly Mar-Nov and was not used.

barley.note: LOW CONFIDENCE for ENSO alignment: chose 'Barley (Spring)' (spring barley dominates US production, ND/MT/ID) whose orange band is two columns ending on the Sep gridline, i.e. Aug-Sep - straddling the Jan-Aug vs Sep-Dec ONI split. Green band left edge is ambiguous between Feb and Mar. 'Barley (Fall)' plants Sep-Dec and harvests May-Jul.

soybeans.note: Green band ~late Apr through Jun; orange Sep-Oct.

wheat.note: Chose 'Wheat (Winter)' - winter wheat is ~70% of US wheat production. Orange left edge sits on the Jun/Jul gridline so harvest may start in Jun. 'Wheat (Spring)' plants Apr-May and harvests Aug-Sep.

rice.note: Image shows five rice rows and nothing else. Chose Rice (Early Spring) = the Dong Xuan winter-spring crop, the largest of Vietnam's rice seasons (~45% of production): green Oct only, grey Nov-Jan, orange Feb. Other rows: Rice (Late Spring) plant Feb-Mar / harvest May; Rice (Early Autumn) plant Feb-Mar / harvest Jun; Rice (Late Autumn) plant Jul-Aug / harvest Nov-Dec; Rice (Winter) plant Jun-Aug / harvest Nov-Dec. Note the seasons straddle the Jan-Aug vs Sep-Dec ONI split.

corn.note: Chose Corn (West) row (Free State/North West, the larger share of national maize): plant Dec-Jan, harvest Jun-Jul (orange band is ~1 column wide centred on Jun, so Jul edge is uncertain). Corn (East) row plants Oct-Nov and harvests Apr-May. Both readings fall in the Jan-Aug ONI bucket.

millet.note: Green band starts around Sep; orange band ~May-Jul, left edge ambiguous between Apr and May.

sorghum.note: Main 'Sorghum' row. Separate 'Sorghum (West)' row harvests ~Apr-Jun with same Dec-Jan planting.

soybeans.note: Green band right edge reaches Dec; left edge ambiguous Oct/Nov, took the conservative Nov.

wheat.note: Winter wheat, Western Cape dominant. Orange band Oct-Nov, may touch early Dec.
